statement: You are given two strings, source and target. A subsequence is what remains after deleting zero or more characters without changing the order of the rest.
Count the ways to choose positions in source whose characters, read in order, spell target. Two ways are different if they use a different set of positions.

examples.explanation: source has three b's and target needs two, so any one of the three b's can be left out.
There are 5 different ways to pick a "b", then a later "a", then a later "g".
